Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High

ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037") or SHA1 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037") or MD5 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037") or SHA1 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037") or MD5 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] FireAnt Metakit supply-chain: update binary spawning unusual child
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — OceanLotus: From external espionage to domestic targeting
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] SPECTRALVIPER known-sample SHA1 execution or filesystem write · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] OceanLotus SPECTRALVIPER C2 connection to ESET-disclosed IPs/domains · [LLM] First-seen connection to recently-registered SPECTRALVIPER-shape C2 domain · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains · DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
OceanLotus SPECTRALVIPER C2 connection to ESET-disclosed IPs/domains AICommand & Control Medium
Alerts on any outbound network connection to the eight SPECTRALVIPER C2 IPs and six C&C domains ESET published for OceanLotus's 2024-2026 FireAnt Metakit supply-chain and Vietnamese construction-corp campaigns. High-fidelity because every IOC is a known-bad C2 endpoint with no documented benign use. Rationale: Every IP and domain in this query is a SPECTRALVIPER C&C endpoint published in ESET's Table 2 and IOC bundle for the 2024-2026 OceanLotus campaigns; financemachinelearning.com is explicitly named as the C&C domain for the stable SPECTRALVIPER variant. Match by IP catches direct fallback; match by URL catches HTTPS proxied through hostname.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sandbox / malware-analysis VM intentionally detonating SPECTRALVIPER samples
  • Threat-intel scrapers / Shodan-style researchers actively probing the IOC set
  • Security-tool URL-categorization scans of the malicious domains (e.g. Zscaler, Netskope)
  • Legitimate hosts that happen to be on a shared-IP CDN that now resolves to one of these IPs (rare — most IOCs are bare hosting)
  • DNS sinkhole responses if these domains have been sinkholed by a TI provider
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "C:\\Program Files\\" or InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msedge.exe","chrome.exe","firefox.exe","iexplore.exe")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: pull the full process tree from DeviceProcessEvents for InitiatingProcessFileName at the time of the connection — confirm whether the originator is a known good binary (security tooling, sandbox) or an unsigned binary in a temp/AppData path matching SPECTRALVIPER drop patterns. 2) CONTAIN: isolate the device via Defender Live Response or EDR network-isolation, block the matched IP/domain at firewall and EDR network indicator policy, force credential reset for the InitiatingProcessAccountName. 3) HUNT: pivot on DeviceFileEvents for SHA1 against the 20-hash IOC set; query DnsEvents for the other five C&C domains across all hosts in the last 90 days; search for any FireAnt Metakit installs (file path or process name) on neighboring hosts and check their update history for a malicious payload window of Oct-2025 to Mar-2026.

let ioc_domains = dynamic(["financemachinelearning.com","gatewayrvcenter.com","coachcybersecurity.com","mxprodesign.com","power-sync-services.com","leadingfilipinoteams.com"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(90d)
| where RemoteIP in (ioc_ips) or RemoteUrl has_any (ioc_domains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let ioc_ips = dynamic(["139.180.128.42","139.99.33.239","166.88.77.186","103.119.47.104","139.162.11.152","142.91.98.77","38.60.245.37","194.68.26.241"]);
let ioc_domains = dynamic(["financemachinelearning.com","gatewayrvcenter.com","coachcybersecurity.com","mxprodesign.com","power-sync-services.com","leadingfilipinoteams.com"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)

  | project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, DstHostname, Url, EventProduct),
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
  | where DestinationIP in (ioc_ips) or DestinationHostName in~ (ioc_domains) or RequestURL has_any (ioc_domains)
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceHostName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, DeviceVendor)

SPECTRALVIPER known-sample SHA1 execution or filesystem write AIInstallation High
Alerts whenever a process executes or a file is written whose SHA1 matches one of the 20 SPECTRALVIPER / OceanLotus stager and dropper hashes ESET published. Covers both SPECTRALVIPER backdoor binaries and the malicious FireAnt Metakit update payloads from the supply-chain wave. Rationale: All 20 SHA1s are pulled directly from the IOC block of the ESET report and correspond to SPECTRALVIPER samples (both old reused first-iteration samples and fresh stable-version samples from Table 1) plus the FireAnt Metakit supply-chain droppers. Hash match on process + filesystem + image-load catches dropper, persistent loader, and DLL side-load variants.
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1027 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Defender / CrowdStrike sample-submission VMs ingesting the IOC bundle for testing
  • DFIR teams replaying confirmed malware samples during tabletop exercises
  • VirusTotal / hybrid-analysis collector hosts that store hash archives
  • Security researcher endpoints reverse-engineering the samples
  • Backup/restore restoring a previously-quarantined sample from shadow copy
Suppression filter
| where DeviceName !has "sandbox" and DeviceName !has "malware" and DeviceName !has "detonation"
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: identify whether the host is a known malware-analysis sandbox or a production endpoint — check device tags, OU membership and the user profile of InitiatingProcessAccountName. If production, this is a confirmed-malicious detection with no investigation needed before action. 2) CONTAIN: network-isolate the device, kill the process tree, quarantine the binary, force credential rotation for any account with an interactive logon to that host in the last 90 days, and block the SHA1 across the EDR fleet via Indicators of Compromise policy. 3) HUNT: for every host that ran one of these hashes, pull DeviceNetworkEvents and DnsEvents 30 days back looking for the six SPECTRALVIPER C2 domains and eight IPs; check FireAnt Metakit install history; pivot on the InitiatingProcessFolderPath to identify the dropper that wrote the sample.

FireAnt Metakit supply-chain: update binary spawning unusual child AIDelivery Medium
Hunts for the FireAnt Metakit application (the Vietnamese stock-investment platform whose update server OceanLotus compromised from Oct-2025 to Mar-2026) spawning script interpreters, LOLBins, or unsigned binaries from temp/AppData. This is the textbook detection shape for the supply-chain payload that ESET observed delivering SPECTRALVIPER after a poisoned update. Rationale: ESET explicitly names FireAnt Metakit as the compromised stock-trading platform and describes the update-server-replaced-with-malicious-payload pattern; any FireAnt Metakit process spawning a script interpreter, LOLBin, or binary out of temp/AppData is the operational shape of the supply-chain payload chain that ends in SPECTRALVIPER drop. Hunting tier because FireAnt's own update process may legitimately invoke some installer LOLBins on first install.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate FireAnt Metakit update invoking msiexec.exe during a real product update
  • FireAnt installer writing helper binaries to %TEMP% as part of normal first-run installation
  • Endpoint backup software (Veeam, Acronis) interacting with FireAnt install directory during scheduled backup
  • User troubleshooting FireAnt by running it from a portable/extracted location in Downloads
  • Antivirus / DLP scanning FireAnt binaries on a schedule and reading from AppData
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessSignatureStatus != "Valid" or ChildSHA256 !in~ (toscalar(DeviceFileCertificateInfo | where IsSigned == true and SignatureType == "CodeSign" | summarize make_set(SHA256)))
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: pull the FireAnt Metakit installer SHA256 and version from InitiatingProcessSHA256 / VersionInfoProductVersion and compare against the vendor's published known-good hash; check the timestamp against ESET's Oct-2025 to Mar-2026 supply-chain window — any install in that range is suspect by default. 2) CONTAIN: if the parent SHA256 is unknown or in the known-bad set, isolate the host, kill the process tree, and quarantine all files written by the child process in the prior 24h; alert the user to discontinue use of FireAnt Metakit pending vendor confirmation. 3) HUNT: query DeviceNetworkEvents on the host for any of the six SPECTRALVIPER C2 domains in the 7 days after the install; pivot DeviceFileEvents for files written by InitiatingProcessFolderPath of FireAnt to identify dropped stagers; check for any other endpoints in the org running FireAnt and audit their install times.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(90d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has "fireant" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("FireAnt","Metakit") or InitiatingProcessParentFileName has "fireant"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","msiexec.exe")
   or FolderPath has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Roaming\", @"\ProgramData\", @"\Windows\Temp\", @"\Users\Public\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ParentSHA256 = InitiatingProcessSHA256,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          ChildSHA256 = SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
| where ParentProcessName has "fireant" or ActingProcessName has_any ("FireAnt","Metakit") or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("FireAnt","Metakit")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetProcessName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","msiexec.exe")
   or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Roaming\", @"\ProgramData\", @"\Windows\Temp\", @"\Users\Public\")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, SHA1, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

id: 9f1c5e22-3a7d-4f44-8e91-2f4a8b9c0d11
description: Detects the FireAnt Metakit Vietnamese stock-investment platform spawning script interpreters, LOLBins, or binaries from temp/AppData. ESET attributes a compromised-update-server supply-chain attack (Oct 2025 - Mar 2026) on this product to OceanLotus / APT32 that resulted in SPECTRALVIPER deployment.
references:
  - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/oceanlotus-external-espionage-domestic-targeting/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/17
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  parent:
    ParentImage|contains:
      - 'FireAnt'
      - 'Metakit'
  suspicious_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'
      - '\regsvr32.exe'
      - '\certutil.exe'
      - '\bitsadmin.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\wget.exe'
      - '\msiexec.exe'
  suspicious_path:
    Image|contains:
      - '\AppData\Local\Temp\'
      - '\AppData\Roaming\'
      - '\ProgramData\'
      - '\Windows\Temp\'
      - '\Users\Public\'
  condition: parent and (suspicious_child or suspicious_path)
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) @EventID:(1 OR 4688) (@ParentImage:(*FireAnt* OR *fireant* OR *Metakit* OR *metakit*) OR @ParentCommandLine:(*FireAnt* OR *fireant* OR *Metakit*)) (@Image:(*\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\cmd.exe OR *\wscript.exe OR *\cscript.exe OR *\mshta.exe OR *\rundll32.exe OR *\regsvr32.exe OR *\certutil.exe OR *\bitsadmin.exe OR *\curl.exe OR *\wget.exe OR *\msiexec.exe) OR @Image:(*\AppData\Local\Temp\* OR *\AppData\Roaming\* OR *\ProgramData\* OR *\Windows\Temp\* OR *\Users\Public\*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/fireant|metakit/i OR ParentImageFileName=/(FireAnt|Metakit)/i
| (ImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh|cmd|wscript|cscript|mshta|rundll32|regsvr32|certutil|bitsadmin|curl|wget|msiexec)\.exe$/i OR regex("\\\\(AppData\\\\Local\\\\Temp|AppData\\\\Roaming|ProgramData|Windows\\\\Temp|Users\\\\Public)\\\\", field=ImageFileName))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name="*fireant*" OR Processes.parent_process="*FireAnt*" OR Processes.parent_process="*Metakit*") AND (Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe") OR Processes.process_path IN ("*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*","*\\AppData\\Roaming\\*","*\\ProgramData\\*","*\\Windows\\Temp\\*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_path Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name="*fireant*" OR Processes.parent_process="*FireAnt*" OR Processes.parent_process="*Metakit*") AND (Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe") OR Processes.process_path IN ("*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*","*\\AppData\\Roaming\\*","*\\ProgramData\\*","*\\Windows\\Temp\\*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_path Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
First-seen connection to recently-registered SPECTRALVIPER-shape C2 domain AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts for any internal host making a first-time HTTPS connection to a domain matching the SPECTRALVIPER C&C naming pattern ESET catalogued (single-word .com domains posing as services - finance/cyber/sync/design themed), where the domain is unseen across the org's 30-day baseline. Designed to catch the next OceanLotus C2 rotation before the IOC list updates. Rationale: Uses the explicit six SPECTRALVIPER C&C domains from ESET Table 2 AND a baseline anti-join so any first-time-in-org connection to a similarly-shaped domain (finance/cyber/services themed single-word .coms — the OceanLotus naming convention) gets flagged. Catches IOC rotation that won't be in the next ESET update.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1568 T1583.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Marketing/finance department visiting a newly-launched legitimate fintech site for the first time
  • User clicking a phishing-link analysis service that proxies through similar-shape domains
  • Threat-intel browser extension fetching from a sandbox URL
  • Internal CI/CD reaching a newly-provisioned vendor SaaS subdomain
  • Domain typosquats of legitimate companies (separate detection class)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msedge.exe","chrome.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","iexplore.exe","safari.exe","opera.exe")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: enrich the matched domain with WHOIS / registration date and passive DNS - any domain registered in the last 90 days with low passive-DNS history and matching the SPECTRALVIPER naming theme is high-suspicion; check InitiatingProcessFileName to see whether it's a browser (often FP) or an unsigned binary (almost always TP). 2) CONTAIN: if non-browser process or unsigned binary, isolate the host, sinkhole the domain via DNS RPZ, and block at proxy/firewall; if browser, push the URL to your secure-browsing/SWG block-list pending vendor categorization. 3) HUNT: across the fleet, search the last 90 days for any prior connection to the same domain or any of the six known SPECTRALVIPER C&Cs; pivot on the matched host for any of the 20 SHA1 SPECTRALVIPER hashes and for FireAnt Metakit install activity.
let BaselineDomains = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp between (ago(30d) .. ago(1d))
    | where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
    | extend Domain = tolower(tostring(split(RemoteUrl, "/")[2]))
    | summarize HostCount = dcount(DeviceId) by Domain
    | where HostCount > 2;
let ioc_pattern = @"(?i)(financemachinelearning|gatewayrvcenter|coachcybersecurity|mxprodesign|power-sync-services|leadingfilipinoteams)\.com$";
let shape_pattern = @"(?i)\b(finance|cyber|sync|design|machinelearning|filipino|gateway|rvcenter|prodesign|services|teams)\b";
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend Domain = tolower(tostring(split(RemoteUrl, "/")[2]))
| where Domain matches regex ioc_pattern or Domain matches regex shape_pattern
| join kind=leftanti BaselineDomains on Domain
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, Domain, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let BaselineDomains = ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(30d) .. ago(1d))
    | summarize HostCount = dcount(SrcIpAddr) by DnsQuery=tolower(DnsQuery)
    | where HostCount > 2;
let ioc_known = dynamic(["financemachinelearning.com","gatewayrvcenter.com","coachcybersecurity.com","mxprodesign.com","power-sync-services.com","leadingfilipinoteams.com"]);
let shape_pattern = @"(?i)\b(finance|cyber|sync|design|machinelearning|filipino|gateway|rvcenter|prodesign|services|teams)\b";
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| extend DnsQueryLower = tolower(DnsQuery)
| where DnsQueryLower has_any (ioc_known) or DnsQueryLower matches regex shape_pattern
| join kind=leftanti BaselineDomains on $left.DnsQueryLower == $right.DnsQuery
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, DnsResponseName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.defender) @EventID:22 (@QueryName:(*financemachinelearning.com OR *gatewayrvcenter.com OR *coachcybersecurity.com OR *mxprodesign.com OR *power-sync-services.com OR *leadingfilipinoteams.com))
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest
| DomainName=/(financemachinelearning|gatewayrvcenter|coachcybersecurity|mxprodesign|power-sync-services|leadingfilipinoteams)\.com$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName, FirstIP4Record], function=count(), function=min(@timestamp))
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where DNS.query IN ("*financemachinelearning.com","*gatewayrvcenter.com","*coachcybersecurity.com","*mxprodesign.com","*power-sync-services.com","*leadingfilipinoteams.com") OR DNS.query="*" by DNS.src DNS.query | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` | join type=left query [ | tstats summariesonly=true earliest(_time) as firstSeenOrg from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where earliest=-30d@d latest=-1d@d by DNS.query | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` ] | where isnull(firstSeenOrg) AND (match(query,"(?i)(finance|cyber|sync|design|machinelearning|filipino|gateway|rvcenter|prodesign).*\.com$")) | sort 0 -count
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where DNS.query IN ("*financemachinelearning.com","*gatewayrvcenter.com","*coachcybersecurity.com","*mxprodesign.com","*power-sync-services.com","*leadingfilipinoteams.com") OR DNS.query="*" by DNS.src DNS.query | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` | join type=left query [ | tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) as firstSeenOrg from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where earliest=-30d@d latest=-1d@d by DNS.query | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` ] | where isnull(firstSeenOrg) AND (match(query,"(?i)(finance|cyber|sync|design|machinelearning|filipino|gateway|rvcenter|prodesign).*\.com$")) | sort 0 -count
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("139.162.11.152", "142.91.98.77", "139.180.128.42", "139.99.33.239", "166.88.77.186", "103.119.47.104", "38.60.245.37", "194.68.26.241") or RemoteUrl has_any ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["139.162.11.152", "142.91.98.77", "139.180.128.42", "139.99.33.239", "166.88.77.186", "103.119.47.104", "38.60.245.37", "194.68.26.241"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:
        DestinationHostname:
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    condition: selection_ip or selection_domain
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive IOC match
level: critical
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("139.162.11.152", "142.91.98.77", "139.180.128.42", "139.99.33.239", "166.88.77.186", "103.119.47.104", "38.60.245.37", "194.68.26.241")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("139.162.11.152", "142.91.98.77", "139.180.128.42", "139.99.33.239", "166.88.77.186", "103.119.47.104", "38.60.245.37", "194.68.26.241")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries Command & Control Medium
Long subdomain labels + frequent queries to a single 2LD = DNS C2/exfil.
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1048.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemotePort == 53 and isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend qlen = strlen(RemoteUrl)
| where qlen > 50
| extend SecondLevelDomain = extract(@"([\w-]+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,})$", 1, RemoteUrl)
| summarize qcount = count(), uniqueSubs = dcount(RemoteUrl), maxLabel = max(qlen)
    by DeviceName, SecondLevelDomain
| where qcount > 100 and uniqueSubs > 20
| order by qcount desc
// ASIM ImDnsActivity normalises Windows DNS, Sysmon EID 22, Linux dnsmasq, etc.
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where DnsQueryTypeName == "TXT"
| summarize Queries = count(), DistinctNames = dcount(DnsQuery)
            by SrcIpAddr, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where Queries > 200    // tune to TXT-query baseline for environment
| order by Queries desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard Installation High
ConnectWise / AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installed outside IT change windows = common tradecraft for ransomware affiliates and IT-helpdesk impersonators.
ATT&CKT1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe")
   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)kaseya.*\.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\AnyDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer_Service.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\atera_agent.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\SplashtopStreamer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\RustDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\NinjaOne.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Remote-Management (RMM) Tool Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0c
status: experimental
description: |
    AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera / Splashtop /
    RustDesk — RMM tools attackers commonly install for hands-on-
    keyboard access. Filter against the IT estate's known tool.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1219/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1219
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\AnyDesk.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer_Service.exe'
            - '\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe'
            - '\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe'
            - '\atera_agent.exe'
            - '\SplashtopStreamer.exe'
            - '\RustDesk.exe'
            - '\NinjaOne.exe'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - IT-approved RMM in use across the estate. Maintain a known-IT-
      tool exclusion list per environment.
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["D511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39F", "59A8553A4F8130F576AB234E0B220BE4D4DA0E98", "9CA1A5C7F79882DB913534C1E62B26BCDCB9F6DD", "A8E2BBBFCB86500322D2367744FA12755AB0C165", "F74F1FEB62B662CDA489FDB2453727824E55ACB9", "F8F8209987CA7F139DE6A62F9E6EE21BD2AE93A9", "19A69F856EFA811C376F68E4FEB0997B4724F8BD", "490194E9BB5128ECA8693AD9E610891C2ED185AF", "51176139B0B2220B802C1578A4994DF68DF5BCD1", "91F042F59BE4BDCB6E5EA21B91DECD731C175B54", "A177ED0BFFEB1EFE1D9D31D72A82EF2625AE646D", "B7B2D2DB544F9EEA74453CDF2B8BEEA58CF07C48", "4AD36AD6C165B5174967020CB1A3358F78D7A283", "57352B3CEEE32216E5AA20BAA848483D7AB5A6FB", "9BC06DF9F932746A05EE728C8B103BD3BA6BF395", "865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "41CB8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B0", "0037DBB0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D20", "5D6194BB48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918B", "B028E947150764A71DEEF498DE6F8C95ECCCB445"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: File or Process Matching Article Hash IOCs
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0b
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__HASH_LIST__` placeholder with article-specific SHA256
    values. Use a watchlist or external indicator file for management
    at scale.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Hashes|contains:
            - 'SHA256=__HASH_PLACEHOLDER_REPLACE_ME__'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive hash match
level: critical
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

GitHub to Disable npm Install Scripts by Default to Stop Supply Chain Attacks

The Hacker News
2026-06-11 11 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

GitHub has announced what it said are "breaking changes" coming to npm version 12, one of which turns off install scripts by default to combat software supply chain threats. The changes aim to combat attack techniques that abuse the "npm install" command to trigger the execution of malicious code using npm lifecycle hooks. "Npm install" is used to download and install all the necessary

npm install lifecycle script spawns interpreter or network-fetcher child AIInstallation Medium
Detects suspicious interpreter or downloader children of npm.exe / node.exe during package install — the exact lifecycle-script code-execution surface GitHub is disabling by default in npm 12. The article specifically names preinstall, install, and postinstall scripts (plus implicit node-gyp rebuilds) as the abuse vector. Rationale: Article names preinstall/install/postinstall lifecycle scripts and implicit node-gyp rebuild as the largest npm code-execution surface. Parent-process pivot (npm/node) plus interpreter/downloader child is the canonical shape of recent npm supply-chain payloads (e.g. recent Microsoft GitHub repo worm). Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/github-to-disable-npm-install-scripts.html • https://github.blog/changelog/
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1059.003 T1195.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate native-addon builds where postinstall invokes node-gyp which shells out to cmd.exe and python
  • Developer-owned packages whose preinstall scripts legitimately curl down a binary asset (e.g. puppeteer Chromium, esbuild prebuilt)
  • CI runners where npm install routinely spawns powershell/bash wrappers for cross-platform scripts
  • electron-builder / node-pre-gyp pulling prebuilt binaries on first install
  • Yarn/pnpm wrappers re-invoking npm under the hood and chaining shell calls
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "node-gyp" and ChildImage endswith "\\cmd.exe" and ChildCmd has_any ("python","msbuild")) | where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("puppeteer","playwright","esbuild","node-pre-gyp","electron") and ChildCmd has_any ("https://","download"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full process tree and InitiatingProcessCommandLine; identify the package being installed by checking CWD for package.json/package-lock.json and which dependency owns the running install hook (npm logs at %APPDATA%\npm-cache\_logs). 2) Contain: isolate the host, revoke any npm/GitHub auth tokens present on it (npm token list, gh auth status), and freeze CI runners that share the registry. 3) Hunt: pivot on the package name + version across the fleet, query for the same parent->child shape in the last 30 days, check npm registry advisories and ThreatFox for that package, and inspect ~/.npmrc and project .npmrc for unexpected registry or authToken entries.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","npm.cmd") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","npm ci","npm i ","npm rebuild","node-gyp rebuild")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ParentImage=InitiatingProcessFolderPath, ParentCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ChildImage=FolderPath, ChildCmd=ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\\npm.exe","\\node.exe","\\npm.cmd") or CommandLine has_any ("npm install","npm ci","npm rebuild","node-gyp rebuild")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","\\cmd.exe","\\wscript.exe","\\cscript.exe","\\mshta.exe","\\rundll32.exe","\\curl.exe","\\wget.exe","\\bitsadmin.exe","\\certutil.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, ParentProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\npm.exe OR *\\NPM.EXE OR *\\node.exe OR *\\NODE.EXE OR *\\npm.cmd) @Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\\cmd.exe OR *\\CMD.EXE OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\mshta.exe OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\certutil.exe OR *\\bitsadmin.exe OR *\\rundll32.exe)

npm install with --allow-git / --allow-remote / --allow-scripts bypass flag AIWeaponization High
Detects explicit use of the new npm 12 allow-list flags (--allow-git, --allow-remote, --allow-scripts) or .npmrc allowScripts=true, which re-open the very code-execution paths GitHub is closing by default. After upgrade, routine use of these flags on developer endpoints is an adversary tell. Rationale: Article calls out --allow-git as the post-v12 opt-in for Git dependencies and --allow-remote for remote URL tarballs, plus the explicit allowScripts default flip. Article also notes the .npmrc-overrides-Git-executable bypass — these flags are the literal strings to grep for. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/github-to-disable-npm-install-scripts.html • https://docs.npmjs.com/cli
ATT&CKT1562.001 T1195.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A senior dev who explicitly trusts and runs a Git dependency with --allow-git for one-off prototyping
  • Internal monorepo tooling that legitimately needs --allow-remote for an internal-only tarball mirror
  • CI pipelines that intentionally set allowScripts=true for native-addon builds (e.g. binding.gyp packages)
  • Vendor build steps invoked by Yarn/pnpm that pass the flags through to nested npm calls
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("\\actions-runner\\","\\agent\\","\\TeamCity\\","\\Jenkins\\","\\gitlab-runner\\") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "node-gyp")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the package and registry being installed - check the CWD, package.json, and any --registry argument on the same command line. Pull npm-cli logs from %APPDATA%\npm-cache\_logs. 2) Contain: if the package is from a public/unknown registry, isolate the host and block the registry FQDN at egress; freeze any artifact built by this run. 3) Hunt: search the fleet for the same package name + version with these flags; look for follow-on outbound connections from node.exe / npm.exe to non-corporate IPs within 10 minutes; check .npmrc files org-wide for allowScripts=true or registry overrides.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","npm.cmd") or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","npm.cmd")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--allow-git","--allow-remote","--allow-scripts","allowScripts=true","allowScripts = true")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\\npm.exe","\\node.exe","\\npm.cmd") or ParentProcessName has_any ("\\npm.exe","\\node.exe")
| where CommandLine has_any ("--allow-git","--allow-remote","--allow-scripts","allowScripts=true","allowScripts = true")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, ParentProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

npm install pointing at non-default registry via --registry or config AIDelivery Medium
Hunts npm/node invocations that point at a registry other than npmjs.org or known mirrors — the canonical dependency-confusion / typosquatting setup, and the path an attacker uses once they have a foothold to redirect a developer to a malicious mirror. Pairs with the v12 install-script hardening: an attacker losing scripts will pivot to redirecting the registry itself. Rationale: Article frames npm install as the supply-chain entry point and v12 closes the script-execution path; redirecting the registry is the natural pivot left to attackers. Non-default --registry is a textbook dependency-confusion precursor and is high-signal on developer endpoints (org-approved registries are usually known). Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/github-to-disable-npm-install-scripts.html
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1584.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developers using an internal Verdaccio / Artifactory / Nexus / GitHub Packages mirror
  • Open-source contributors pointing at a forked registry for testing a new feature
  • CI runners configured with a corporate mirror that fronts npmjs.org
  • One-off install from a vendor-provided registry during a POC
  • Yarn invocations that pass --registry through to nested npm calls
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("verdaccio","artifactory","nexus","npm.pkg.github.com","jfrog","myget") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("\\actions-runner\\","\\Jenkins\\","\\TeamCity\\","\\agent\\"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: extract the registry URL from the command line and resolve it - check WHOIS, certificate transparency, and the org's approved-mirror list. Look at the package(s) being installed in the same command. 2) Contain: if the registry is not on the approved list, isolate the host and block the FQDN at egress; quarantine any node_modules built during this run. 3) Hunt: pivot on the registry FQDN across DeviceNetworkEvents for the last 30 days; check whether other developers / CI runners hit the same URL; query for follow-on outbound connections from node.exe within 5 minutes of the install.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","npm.cmd") or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","npm.cmd")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "--registry" or ProcessCommandLine has "config set registry"
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "registry.npmjs.org"
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "registry.yarnpkg.com"
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "registry.npmmirror.com"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\\npm.exe","\\node.exe","\\npm.cmd")
| where CommandLine has "--registry" or CommandLine has "config set registry"
| where CommandLine !has "registry.npmjs.org"
| where CommandLine !has "registry.yarnpkg.com"
| where CommandLine !has "registry.npmmirror.com"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
