Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] KEV exposure sweep — CVE-2026-20245 (Cisco SD-WAN), CVE-2026-11645 (Chrome V8), CVE-2026-7473 (Arista EOS) · Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Chrome renderer spawns non-browser child — possible V8 sandbox escape (CVE-2026-11645) · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
KEV exposure sweep — CVE-2026-20245 (Cisco SD-WAN), CVE-2026-11645 (Chrome V8), CVE-2026-7473 (Arista EOS) AIReconnaissance High
Surface every managed endpoint / network device that Defender TVM has flagged as carrying one of the three CVEs CISA added to KEV on 2026-06-10. Drives the FCEB 2026-06-23 remediation deadline and identifies the population an attacker is most likely to target next. Rationale: Directly anchored on the three CVE IDs CISA published in the article body. No behavioural inference — pure inventory pivot against MDE TVM telemetry. Pairs the result with internet-facing context so the SOC can prioritise the externally-reachable Cisco SD-WAN Managers and Arista 7020R/7280R/7500R switches the article calls out. Cross-checked CISA KEV catalog as authoritative source for the CVE list. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog • https://www.arista.com/en/support/advisories-notices/security-advisory
ATT&CKT1190 T1203
Data sourcesVulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Decommissioned device still present in TVM inventory (stale agent check-in)
  • TVM scanner misattributes CVE to a sibling SoftwareVersion (verify exact build)
  • Affected device sits behind an upstream ACL already mitigating CVE-2026-7473 — compensating control in place
  • Chrome devices that auto-updated since last TVM sync but the inventory hasn't refreshed
  • Cisco SD-WAN Manager in an isolated mgmt VRF where the 'authenticated local' precondition is impractical
Suppression filter
| where SoftwareVersion !in~ ("<add-confirmed-patched-builds-here>")
Response runbook
Step 1 — triage: for each hit, confirm the live software version on the device (vmanage show version / chrome://settings/help / show version on Arista) matches what TVM reports; rule out stale inventory. Cross-reference IsInternetFacing and exposure path. Step 2 — contain: for Chrome push the patched build via Intune/policy and force restart; for Cisco SD-WAN Manager apply the vendor fix per cisco-sa advisory; for Arista 7020R/7280R/7500R apply upstream-or-device ACLs that allow only legitimate tunnel sources to the configured VTEP/GRE/decap-group IP (no patch is planned). Step 3 — hunt: on every affected host run the companion Chrome-V8 child-spawn hunt (UC2) and pull DeviceNetworkEvents for unexpected tunnel traffic to Arista VTEP IPs in the last 30 days.

Chrome renderer spawns non-browser child — possible V8 sandbox escape (CVE-2026-11645) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts the post-condition of a successful Chrome V8 OOB read/write exploit chained with a sandbox escape: chrome.exe parenting a non-Chrome child process (shell, LOLBin, script host). CVE-2026-11645 alone lands inside the renderer sandbox, so any non-sandbox child of chrome.exe is the smoke from a full chain. Rationale: Article specifically says CVE-2026-11645 is an OOB RCE 'inside a sandbox' — so a single-bug exploit cannot leave the renderer process. Anything observed as a non-Chrome child of chrome.exe in user-context means the chain reached a second bug (sandbox escape). LOLBin/temp-path/encoded-PowerShell narrows it to attacker-shaped children rather than benign native-messaging helpers. Cross-checked CISA KEV catalog confirming active exploitation as of 2026-06-10. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog • https://chromereleases.googleblog.com/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1203/
ATT&CKT1203 T1189 T1059
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Password manager / enterprise SSO native messaging host launching a signed helper from %LOCALAPPDATA%
  • Chrome auto-update spawning setup.exe / GoogleUpdate.exe (already in the exclude list — watch for renames)
  • Print-to-PDF or 'Open with' integrations launching a signed third-party viewer
  • DLP / endpoint-protection agents that hook chrome.exe and inject rundll32 in user context
  • Webex / Teams / Zoom one-click meeting launchers when invoked from a calendar link rendered in Chrome
Suppression filter
| where not (ChildLower == "rundll32.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("davclnt.dll,DavSetCookie", "shell32.dll,Control_RunDLL"))
| where not (FolderPath startswith @"C:\Program Files\" and InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName has "Google LLC")
Response runbook
Step 1 — triage: pull the parent chrome.exe command line — does it carry a `--type=renderer` flag with a URL? Pivot URL through threat intel and look at UrlClickEvents for the user in the prior 5 minutes. Confirm child SHA256 is not a known enterprise helper. Step 2 — contain: isolate the device via Defender Live Response, terminate the chrome.exe tree, force-deploy the patched Chrome stable build through Intune/SCCM. Reset the user's session cookies. Step 3 — hunt: on the same host pull DeviceNetworkEvents and DeviceFileEvents in a 30-minute window around the child spawn — look for second-stage download (a new EXE/DLL written to Temp by the child, or a non-CDN outbound to a fresh domain). Pivot the child SHA256 + cmdline pattern across the fleet.
let chrome_known_children = dynamic(["chrome.exe","chrome_proxy.exe","chrome_crashpad_handler.exe","chrome_pwa_launcher.exe","elevation_service.exe","setup.exe","googleupdate.exe","goopdate.dll","notification_helper.exe"]);
let lolbins = dynamic(["cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","installutil.exe","msbuild.exe","forfiles.exe","hh.exe","wmic.exe","whoami.exe","net.exe","net1.exe","nltest.exe","systeminfo.exe","ipconfig.exe","tasklist.exe","schtasks.exe","reg.exe","bash.exe","wsl.exe"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "chrome.exe"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| extend ChildLower = tolower(FileName)
| where ChildLower !in (chrome_known_children)
| where ChildLower in (lolbins)
   or FolderPath has_any (@"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\Users\Public\", @"\ProgramData\", @"\Downloads\")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-EncodedCommand","-enc ","FromBase64String","DownloadString","IEX ","Invoke-Expression")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256, InitiatingProcessIntegrityLevel
| order by Timestamp desc
let known = dynamic(["chrome.exe","chrome_proxy.exe","chrome_crashpad_handler.exe","chrome_pwa_launcher.exe","elevation_service.exe","setup.exe","googleupdate.exe","notification_helper.exe"]);
let lolbins = dynamic(["cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","installutil.exe","msbuild.exe","forfiles.exe","hh.exe","wmic.exe","whoami.exe","net.exe","net1.exe","nltest.exe","systeminfo.exe","ipconfig.exe","tasklist.exe","schtasks.exe","reg.exe","bash.exe","wsl.exe"]);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| extend ParentLower = tolower(tostring(split(ParentProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| extend ChildLower  = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName,    "\\")[-1]))
| where ParentLower == "chrome.exe"
| where ChildLower !in (known)
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| where ChildLower in (lolbins)
   or NewProcessName has_any (@"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\Users\Public\", @"\ProgramData\", @"\Downloads\")
   or CommandLine has_any ("-EncodedCommand","-enc ","FromBase64String","DownloadString","IEX ","Invoke-Expression")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName,
          ParentProcessName, ParentCmd = tostring(parse_xml(EventData)),
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, TokenElevationType
| order by TimeGenerated desc

      - '\systeminfo.exe'
      - '\tasklist.exe'
      - '\schtasks.exe'
      - '\reg.exe'
      - '\bash.exe'

falsepositives:

  - Enterprise Chrome extension launching a signed helper
  - Print-to-PDF / file-download helper utilities
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\chrome.exe OR *\CHROME.EXE) (@Image:(*\cmd.exe OR *\powershell.exe OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\wscript.exe OR *\cscript.exe OR *\mshta.exe OR *\rundll32.exe OR *\regsvr32.exe OR *\certutil.exe OR *\bitsadmin.exe OR *\curl.exe OR *\wget.exe OR *\installutil.exe OR *\msbuild.exe OR *\wmic.exe OR *\bash.exe OR *\wsl.exe) OR @CommandLine:(*-EncodedCommand* OR *FromBase64String* OR *DownloadString* OR *Invoke-Expression*)) -@Image:(*\chrome_proxy.exe OR *\chrome_crashpad_handler.exe OR *\GoogleUpdate.exe OR *\elevation_service.exe) -@User:*$
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^chrome\.exe$/i
| NOT ImageFileName=/\\(chrome|chrome_proxy|chrome_crashpad_handler|chrome_pwa_launcher|GoogleUpdate|elevation_service|setup|notification_helper)\.exe$/i
| NOT UserName=/\$$/
| ImageFileName=/\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|wscript|cscript|mshta|rundll32|regsvr32|certutil|bitsadmin|curl|wget|installutil|msbuild|wmic|whoami|net|net1|nltest|systeminfo|tasklist|schtasks|reg|bash|wsl)\.exe$/i OR regex("(?i)(-EncodedCommand|FromBase64String|DownloadString|Invoke-Expression|IEX )", field=CommandLine) OR regex("(?i)\\\\(Temp|AppData\\\\Local\\\\Temp|Users\\\\Public|ProgramData|Downloads)\\\\", field=ImageFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=count())

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents

| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)

| order by conn_count desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name

status: experimental
description: |

JWT Bearer token with PoC-distinctive far-future expiration (exp=9999999999) AIActions on Objectives High
Detects HTTP requests carrying Authorization: Bearer JWTs whose 'exp' claim decodes to the PoC-distinctive year-2286 value (9999999999). The article's published PoC token hardcodes this expiration, so any token in the wild with this exact exp is a high-fidelity forgery signal against go-base instances. Rationale: The article's PoC hardcodes exp=9999999999. Any production JWT presenting this distinctive far-future expiration against the named go-base admin endpoints is a near-certain forgery indicator. ImWebSession.HttpRequestHeaderAuthorization is the canonical Sentinel field for header inspection — avoids CommonSecurityLog's missing AdditionalExtensions issue. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mqq6-462x-jxmm
ATT&CKT1550.001 T1606.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher / red team replaying the PoC against an internal test instance
  • Developer debugging JWT validation with a hand-crafted long-lived token
  • Automated API test suite using a never-expiring stub token in lower environments
  • Penetration test engagement using the published advisory PoC verbatim
Suppression filter
| where SrcIpAddr !in ("10.0.0.0/8", "192.168.0.0/16")
| where HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent !has_any ("PostmanRuntime", "insomnia", "BurpSuite", "OWASP ZAP")
Response runbook
Triage: Extract the full Authorization header from the request log, base64-decode the JWT payload, and confirm alg=HS256 + the exact exp value. Verify the destination is a go-base instance by checking the response body for the /api/v1/me JSON shape. Contain: Rotate AUTH_JWT_SECRET on the target instance to a 32+ byte random value (`openssl rand -base64 32`), restart the service, invalidate all active refresh tokens. Hunt: Search 30 days back for any Bearer token whose payload contains exp >2^32 seconds in the future or sub claims that don't match a known user; pivot on the source IP for any prior recon traffic to /api/v1/.
// Defender XDR doesn't natively parse Authorization headers; this targets the URL/UA shape
// for go-base admin endpoints and looks for the PoC's literal exp value in command lines
// (curl/wget/python invocations that embed the forged token).
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("/api/v1/admin/users", "/api/v1/me", "/api/v1/token/refresh")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("curl.exe","wget.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","python.exe","python3.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("Bearer", "Authorization")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "9999999999"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName,
          AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          ProcessName=InitiatingProcessFileName,
          CmdLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          RemoteUrl, RemoteIP
| order by Timestamp desc
// Detects JWTs in Authorization headers whose payload decodes to the PoC's hardcoded
// far-future expiration (9999999999 = year 2286). Only the published PoC uses this value.
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where isnotempty(HttpRequestHeaderAuthorization)
| where HttpRequestHeaderAuthorization startswith "Bearer "
| extend Jwt = substring(HttpRequestHeaderAuthorization, 7, 4096)
| extend JwtParts = split(Jwt, ".")
| where array_length(JwtParts) == 3
| extend PayloadB64 = tostring(JwtParts[1])
| extend PayloadB64Padded = strcat(PayloadB64, substring("====", 0, (4 - strlen(PayloadB64) % 4) % 4))
| extend Payload = base64_decode_tostring(replace_string(replace_string(PayloadB64Padded, "-", "+"), "_", "/"))
| where Payload matches regex @"""exp""\s*:\s*99{8,}" or Payload has "9999999999"
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, DstHostname, Url, HttpMethod, HttpStatusCode, Payload, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
(source:nginx OR source:apache OR source:iis OR source:cloudflare OR source:zscaler) @http.url_details.path:("/api/v1/admin/users" OR "/api/v1/me" OR "/api/v1/token/refresh") @http.request.headers.authorization:(*9999999999* OR *9999999000*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 (ImageFileName=/(curl|wget|python3?|powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i OR ImageFileName=/\/(curl|wget|python3?)$/)
| regex("(Authorization|Bearer)", field=CommandLine)
| regex("9999999999", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
# log group: /aws/apigateway/access-logs (CloudFront / API Gateway access logs with header capture)
fields @timestamp, sourceIp, requestParameters.path, requestParameters.headers.Authorization, responseElements.statusCode
| filter requestParameters.path like /\/api\/v1\/(admin|me|token\/refresh)/
      and requestParameters.headers.Authorization like /Bearer/
      and requestParameters.headers.Authorization like /9999999999/
| sort @timestamp desc

Reconnaissance: outbound clone/fetch of github.com/dhax/go-base AIReconnaissance Medium
Detects clones, raw-content fetches, or proxy traffic to github.com/dhax/go-base — the vulnerable repository. Pre-exploitation reconnaissance typically pulls the source to confirm the hardcoded 'random' secret is still present in the target version. Rationale: github.com/dhax/go-base is the specific vulnerable repository named in the GHSA. Sentinel KQL uses each table's canonical host identifier — ImWebSession.DvcHostname, W3CIISLog.Computer, CommonSecurityLog.DeviceAddress — not DeviceName which doesn't exist on the CEF/IIS schemas. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mqq6-462x-jxmm • https://github.com/dhax/go-base/pull/31
ATT&CKT1593.003 T1592.002
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal Go developer browsing the repo for boilerplate ideas
  • SCA / dependency scanner indexing public Go repositories
  • Security awareness training where the advisory is shared internally
  • Blue-team analyst researching this advisory after seeing the alert
  • CI pipeline pulling go-base as an inherited transitive dependency
Suppression filter
| where User !in ("dev-team", "security-research")
| where Host !startswith "dev-" and Host !startswith "build-"
Response runbook
Triage: Pivot on the source host and user — known developer machine, CI runner, or production server with no business fetching public Go repos? Inspect command line: `git clone`, `go get`, or raw `curl` of dev.env (the latter is the highest-signal). Contain: If the source host is production, isolate immediately and check for outbound Authorization: Bearer requests in the next hour. Hunt: For the same host, look 24h ahead for outbound Bearer headers targeting internal go-base instances; 24h backward for `grep AUTH_JWT_SECRET` or similar local enumeration.
union
(DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where RemoteUrl has_any ("github.com/dhax/go-base", "raw.githubusercontent.com/dhax/go-base", "codeload.github.com/dhax/go-base")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, ProcessName=InitiatingProcessFileName, CmdLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP),
(DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where FileName in~ ("git.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","go.exe")
  | where ProcessCommandLine has "dhax/go-base"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessName=FileName, CmdLine=ProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl="", RemoteIP="")
| order by Timestamp desc
// Uses host-identifier columns canonical to each table: ImWebSession.DvcHostname,
// W3CIISLog.Computer, CommonSecurityLog.DeviceAddress (NOT DeviceName — not a column).
let recon_targets = dynamic(["github.com/dhax/go-base", "raw.githubusercontent.com/dhax/go-base", "codeload.github.com/dhax/go-base"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where Url has_any (recon_targets)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, SrcIp=SrcIpAddr, User=SrcUsername, Url, UserAgent=HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, Source="ImWebSession"),
(W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where csUriStem has_any (recon_targets) or csUriQuery has_any (recon_targets) or csReferer has_any (recon_targets)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, SrcIp=cIP, User=csUserName, Url=strcat(csUriStem, "?", csUriQuery), UserAgent=csUserAgent, Source="W3CIISLog"),
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where RequestURL has_any (recon_targets) or DestinationHostName has_any (recon_targets)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host=DeviceAddress, SrcIp=SourceIP, User=SourceUserName, Url=RequestURL, UserAgent=RequestClientApplication, Source="CommonSecurityLog")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

go-base admin endpoint access with Bearer token but no preceding login AIExploitation High
Detects HTTP 2xx responses on the named go-base admin endpoints (/api/v1/admin/users, /api/v1/me, /api/v1/token/refresh) when the same client/user has no successful authentication event in the prior 15 minutes. Token forgery against the hardcoded 'random' secret bypasses the login flow entirely — successful admin access without a corresponding auth event is the signature. Rationale: The article's PoC names the exact endpoints and explicitly demonstrates that a forged token bypasses login. Joining admin-endpoint 2xx responses against absence of prior successful auth catches the gap — a real user would have just authenticated. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mqq6-462x-jxmm
ATT&CKT1550.001 T1078 T1606.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web Authentication.Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Long-lived session where the user authenticated >15 min ago and still holds a valid token
  • Service account / machine identity using a long-lived bearer outside the interactive auth flow
  • Mobile app using refresh tokens that don't generate fresh login events on the same channel
  • API client behind a reverse proxy that strips the original auth event from this telemetry source
  • Healthcheck monitor hitting /api/v1/me with a static service token
Suppression filter
| where SrcUsername !in ("healthcheck-svc", "monitoring-bot", "prometheus-exporter")
Response runbook
Triage: Decode the Authorization Bearer JWT to extract sub, roles, iat, exp claims. Confirm the sub matches a real user and iat is sane (not 9999999000 from the PoC). Verify whether the user has any legitimate interactive session on a different channel. Contain: Revoke all refresh tokens for the affected user immediately and rotate AUTH_JWT_SECRET to a 32-byte random value. If the role is admin and the sub looks fabricated (e.g. admin@example.com from the PoC), treat as confirmed exploitation. Hunt: Query 30 days back for all 2xx responses to /api/v1/admin/* from the same source IP; check whether subsequent /api/v1/token/refresh calls minted additional tokens; audit user-table changes during the access window.
let WindowMin = 15m;
let AdminAccess = DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where RemoteUrl has_any ("/api/v1/admin/users", "/api/v1/me", "/api/v1/token/refresh")
  | project ApiTime=Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP;
let Logons = DeviceLogonEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where ActionType == "LogonSuccess"
  | summarize LastLogon=max(Timestamp) by DeviceName, AccountName;
AdminAccess
| join kind=leftouter Logons on DeviceName, AccountName
| where isnull(LastLogon) or datetime_diff('minute', ApiTime, LastLogon) > 15
| project ApiTime, DeviceName, AccountName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, LastLogon
| order by ApiTime desc
let AdminAccess = ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where Url has_any ("/api/v1/admin/users", "/api/v1/me", "/api/v1/token/refresh")
  | where HttpStatusCode between (200 .. 299)
  | where isnotempty(HttpRequestHeaderAuthorization) and HttpRequestHeaderAuthorization startswith "Bearer "
  | project ApiTime=TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Url, HttpStatusCode;
let Auth = ImAuthentication
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where EventResult == "Success"
  | summarize LastLogon=max(TimeGenerated) by TargetUsername, SrcIpAddr;
AdminAccess
| join kind=leftouter Auth on $left.SrcUsername == $right.TargetUsername, SrcIpAddr
| where isnull(LastLogon) or datetime_diff('minute', ApiTime, LastLogon) > 15
| project ApiTime, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Url, HttpStatusCode, LastLogon
| order by ApiTime desc

go-base process started with known-weak AUTH_JWT_SECRET in environment AIInstallation High
Detects go-base server processes (or `go run cmd/serve`) started with the AUTH_JWT_SECRET environment variable explicitly set to one of the known-weak values PR#31 added to the deny-list — random, secret, changeme, change-me, default, or empty. These instances are actively exploitable for JWT forgery and warrant immediate config remediation. Rationale: The article names the exact config knob (AUTH_JWT_SECRET) and the exact weak values PR#31 added to the deny-list. Any go-base instance launched with one of those values in its environment is, by the maintainer's own post-fix definition, exploitable. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mqq6-462x-jxmm • https://github.com/dhax/go-base/pull/31
ATT&CKT1526 T1078
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Pre-production / lab environment intentionally using the dev.env default
  • CI integration tests setting AUTH_JWT_SECRET=secret to exercise the weak-secret guard
  • Developer running `go run cmd/serve` locally without overriding the default
  • Docker / k8s deployment manifest that copies dev.env verbatim into staging
Suppression filter
| where DvcHostname !startswith "dev-" and DvcHostname !startswith "staging-" and DvcHostname !contains "lab"
Response runbook
Triage: Confirm the affected host is a real internet-facing deployment, not a lab. Identify the deployment vector — .env file, container env var, or k8s Secret — and pull the manifest from config management. Contain: Generate a strong replacement (`openssl rand -base64 32`), update the secret in the deployment manifest / vault, roll the service, and invalidate all currently-issued refresh tokens. Hunt: Pivot on this host's inbound /api/v1/admin/* and /api/v1/token/refresh traffic for the last 30 days; any 2xx responses from external IPs during that window may have been forged-token access.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("go-base","go-base.exe","serve","serve.exe")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("go-base", "cmd/serve")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)AUTH_JWT_SECRET\s*=\s*(random|secret|changeme|change-me|default)\b"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          ParentProcess=InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(^|/|\\)(go-base|serve)(\.exe)?$"
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("go-base", "cmd/serve")

Compromised Rust crate onering performs code exfiltration

Aikido
2026-06-10 8 use cases 3 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

The compromised onering Rust crate v1.4.1 on crates.io shipped a malicious build.rs that exfiltrates the diff of your latest commit to a hosted Sentry endpoint every time you build. Category: Vulnerabilities & Threats

ATT&CKT1176 T1190 T1195.002
Domainso4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io
Click any ATT&CK pill below to open it on the Matrix

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Cargo manifest / lockfile references onering crate
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → Suspicious browser extension installation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound to onering crate C2 Sentry ingest endpoint (o4511539639222272) · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Cargo build-script-build spawning curl/PowerShell to Sentry envelope endpoint · [LLM] Cargo build script harvesting git log/diff (onering build.rs payload) · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
Outbound to onering crate C2 Sentry ingest endpoint (o4511539639222272) AICommand & Control High
Detects DNS resolution or outbound HTTPS to the static Sentry ingest endpoint used as exfiltration sink by the compromised onering 1.4.1 Rust crate. The Sentry org ID o4511539639222272 / project 4511539669368912 are attacker-owned and never appear in legitimate crash reporting. Rationale: Article gives an attacker-specific Sentry org id (o4511539639222272) and project id (4511539669368912) hard-coded into the build.rs payload. Hitting either string in DNS or HTTP egress telemetry is unambiguous — legitimate Sentry users never resolve another organization's ingest subdomain. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/compromised-rust-crate-onering-performs-code-exfiltration • https://github.com/cenotelie/onering/issues/1 • https://crates.io/crates/onering
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1071.001 T1041
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher executing the onering crate inside an analysis sandbox
  • Aikido / vendor reproducing the IOC for blogpost screenshots
  • Threat-intel automation auto-resolving published IOCs for confirmation
  • CI runner that built onering 1.4.1 before the takedown — flag and remediate, not a true FP
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the InitiatingProcess (expected: build-script-build, curl, cargo, rustc). Pull Cargo.lock from the developer/CI host and confirm an entry for `onering = "1.4.1"`. Capture exact git diff that was exfiltrated by retrieving `git log -n 1` and `git diff HEAD^ HEAD` on the affected repo as of the build time. 2) Contain: isolate the host, revoke any source code / SSH / cloud credentials present in the leaked diff, rotate any secrets visible in HEAD~1 commits, pin Cargo.lock back to last-known-good onering (<=1.4.0), and block o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io at egress proxy + DNS RPZ. 3) Hunt: enumerate every repo with `onering` in any Cargo.lock under version control, run UC `Cargo manifest references onering`, and scan CI build logs for prior beacons against the same Sentry org id over the last 90 days.

(DeviceEvents

  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort=int(null), EventTable="DeviceEvents-DNS")
| order by Timestamp desc
let OneringSentryHost = "o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io";
let OneringProjectId = "4511539669368912";
union isfuzzy=true
(ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DnsQuery has OneringSentryHost
  | project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DnsQuery, EventVendor, EventProduct, Source="DNS"),

  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where Url has OneringSentryHost or Url has OneringProjectId
  | project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname=DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DnsQuery=Url, EventVendor, EventProduct, Source="Web"),

  | where DestinationHostName has OneringSentryHost or RequestURL has OneringSentryHost or RequestURL has OneringProjectId

Cargo build-script-build spawning curl/PowerShell to Sentry envelope endpoint AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the onering 1.4.1 process tree where a Cargo build script binary ("build-script-build" under target/.../build/) invokes curl or PowerShell with a sentry.io envelope URL or x-sentry-envelope content-type. Build scripts have no legitimate reason to POST crash telemetry to a third-party Sentry tenant. Rationale: Combines two article-specific anchors: the Cargo target/build/<crate>-<hash>/build-script-build process (the literal binary Cargo emits when compiling a build.rs) AND the attacker-owned Sentry org/project/DSN strings hardcoded in the leaked payload. Either alone is signal; both together is the exact malicious chain described in the article. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/compromised-rust-crate-onering-performs-code-exfiltration • https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/build-scripts.html
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1059 T1041
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Crate maintainer locally testing a Sentry-based crash reporter from inside their own build.rs (rare — Sentry SDKs use SDK clients, not curl shell-outs)
  • Security researcher detonating the onering crate in a sandbox after the disclosure
  • Internal staging of a sentry-mirror endpoint that happens to share a substring with the IOC org id (extremely unlikely)
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full process tree (build-script-build → curl → network), extract the exact Sentry envelope POST body from EDR if available, and identify the consuming repo via the build's target directory path. 2) Contain: kill the cargo/build process on the host, isolate the host from network, pin Cargo.lock to onering <= 1.4.0 (or remove the dep), purge ~/.cargo/registry/cache/*/onering-1.4.1.crate and ~/.cargo/registry/src/*/onering-1.4.1, block egress to *.ingest.de.sentry.io org id o4511539639222272. 3) Hunt: pivot on build-script-build parent process across the fleet over 30 days regardless of URL — find other malicious crates with the same TTP. Run UC1 (Sentry C2 egress) as the cross-check.

      or InitiatingProcessFolderPath matches regex @"(?i)[\\/]target[\\/](debug|release)[\\/]build[\\/].+[\\/]build[-_]script[-_]build")
| where FileName in~ ("curl.exe","curl","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wget.exe","wget")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("sentry.io","x-sentry-envelope","ingest.de.sentry.io","4511539669368912","8197ee42c4f59c83f4cc6d48f5bae821","o4511539639222272")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where (ParentProcessName matches regex @"(?i)build[-_]script[-_]build(\.exe)?$"
      or ParentProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)[\\/]target[\\/](debug|release)[\\/]build[\\/].+[\\/]build[-_]script[-_]build")
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)^(curl|powershell|pwsh|wget)(\.exe)?$"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("sentry.io","x-sentry-envelope","ingest.de.sentry.io","4511539669368912","8197ee42c4f59c83f4cc6d48f5bae821","o4511539639222272")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Cargo manifest / lockfile references onering crate AIDelivery High
Surfaces every host whose Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock pulls in the compromised onering crate (specifically version 1.4.1, but flag any pinned/unpinned reference because the GitHub mirror cenotelie/onering is also compromised). Anchored on the exact crate name from the article. Rationale: The article names the crate by string ("onering") and the compromised version ("1.4.1"), and explicitly states the GitHub source mirror cenotelie/onering is also poisoned — so detection has to cover both registry (cargo add onering) and git-clone vectors. Anchoring on cargo/rustc/git cmdline keeps the query cheap and broadly portable across Win/Linux build hosts. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/compromised-rust-crate-onering-performs-code-exfiltration • https://github.com/cenotelie/onering/issues/1 • https://crates.io/crates/onering
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1199
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Dev pinned to pre-1.4.1 onering and updating Cargo.lock with `cargo update -p onering` — needs version inspection to confirm safe
  • Security team reviewing the malicious crate inside an analysis container
  • Mirror / vendoring service auto-pulling crates.io index updates (e.g. internal cargo mirror crons)
  • IDE auto-completion in rust-analyzer hitting the registry name without actually adding the dep
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the host's Cargo.lock and confirm the resolved `name = "onering"` block — capture the `version` and `source` fields. If version == 1.4.1 OR source contains cenotelie/onering at any commit, treat as confirmed. 2) Contain: roll Cargo.lock back to the last commit prior to onering 1.4.1, run `cargo clean`, purge ~/.cargo/registry/cache/*/onering-1.4.1.crate and the matching src/ extraction, force-rebuild from clean. Rotate any secrets present in HEAD~1 commits because git diff HEAD^ HEAD has already been exfiltrated for every build since the dep landed. 3) Hunt: enumerate every repo across the org with `onering` in Cargo.lock (git grep across mirrored repos) and run UC1 + UC2 on those hosts to confirm whether exfil actually fired.
// Hunt for onering 1.4.1 ingestion via Cargo or git clone
let OneringStrings = dynamic(["onering","cenotelie/onering"]);
let ProcSignals = DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(90d)
  | where (FileName in~ ("cargo.exe","cargo","rustc.exe","rustc") and ProcessCommandLine has_any (OneringStrings))
       or (FileName in~ ("git.exe","git") and ProcessCommandLine has "cenotelie/onering")
       or (ProcessCommandLine has "cargo add" and ProcessCommandLine has "onering")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, EvidenceType="ProcessCmdline";
let FileSignals = DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(90d)
  | where FileName in~ ("Cargo.toml","Cargo.lock")
  | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("cargo.exe","cargo","code.exe","rust-analyzer.exe","rust-analyzer","git.exe","git")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine=FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, EvidenceType="CargoManifestWrite";
union ProcSignals, FileSignals
| order by Timestamp desc
let OneringStrings = dynamic(["onering","cenotelie/onering"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
| where (ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)^(cargo|rustc)(\.exe)?$" and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (OneringStrings))
     or (ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)^git(\.exe)?$" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "cenotelie/onering")
     or (ActingProcessCommandLine has "cargo add" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "onering")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Rust Cargo Resolving Compromised onering Crate

Cargo build script harvesting git log/diff (onering build.rs payload) AIActions on Objectives High
Surfaces the exact git command pair the onering build.rs runs: `git log -n 1 --pretty=format:{"commit":...` and `git diff HEAD^ HEAD`, when the parent process is a Cargo build script binary under target/.../build/. Catches the exfil payload before it ever hits the network. Rationale: Article quotes the literal git invocations verbatim: `git log -n 1 --pretty=format:{"commit":"%H",...}` and `git diff HEAD^ HEAD`. The `--pretty=format:{"commit"` token is extremely specific — virtually no legitimate tooling formats git log as a JSON-object string. Pairing those with the Cargo build-script-build parent narrows to the exact onering build.rs. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/compromised-rust-crate-onering-performs-code-exfiltration • https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/build-scripts.html
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1213.003 T1059
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Custom build.rs that injects git rev / commit hash into the binary via `git rev-parse HEAD` (won't match — different cmdline)
  • Future malicious build script copy-cat using the same TTP (true positive on a different crate, not an FP — investigate the parent)
  • Developer running git log/diff inside a Cargo workspace shell — not from build-script-build parent, so won't match
  • Pre-release rust-analyzer / IDE plugins occasionally invoke git log to render annotations
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("\\onering-1.4.0\\","\\onering-1.4.0-") and ProcessCommandLine has "rev-parse HEAD")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm InitiatingProcessFolderPath resolves under target/.../build/<crate>-<hash>/ and identify <crate>. If <crate> starts with `onering-`, this is the disclosed payload. Pull the consuming repo path from the build script's working directory. 2) Contain: kill the build process, isolate the host, pin Cargo.lock to drop onering, purge ~/.cargo/registry/cache/*/onering-1.4.1.crate and src/, force-rebuild clean. Treat the most-recent committed diff on every affected repo as PUBLIC — rotate any secrets / API keys / customer data visible in `git diff HEAD^ HEAD` from the time of the first matching event onward. 3) Hunt: rerun the query without the cmdline filter (just build-script-build → git) over 90 days to find other crates exhibiting the same harvest TTP, and cross-reference with UC1 to confirm any actually exfiltrated.
// onering build.rs: build-script-build -> git log/diff harvest
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("git.exe","git")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName matches regex @"(?i)^build[-_]script[-_]build(\.exe)?$"
     or InitiatingProcessFolderPath matches regex @"(?i)[\\/]target[\\/](debug|release)[\\/]build[\\/].+[\\/]build[-_]script[-_]build"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("diff HEAD^ HEAD", "--pretty=format:{\"commit\"", "log -n 1")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)^git(\.exe)?$"
| where (ParentProcessName matches regex @"(?i)^build[-_]script[-_]build(\.exe)?$"
      or ParentProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)[\\/]target[\\/](debug|release)[\\/]build[\\/].+[\\/]build[-_]script[-_]build")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("diff HEAD^ HEAD", "--pretty=format:{\"commit\"", "log -n 1")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Cargo Build Script Invoking git diff HEAD^ HEAD (onering Exfil Pattern)
id: 4d6e7f80-5c4b-4eab-bb22-2c3d4e5f6071
description: Detects the exact git harvest commands used by the malicious onering 1.4.1 Rust crate build.rs to capture commit metadata and the textual diff of the consuming repository's latest commit prior to exfiltration.
references:
  - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/compromised-rust-crate-onering-performs-code-exfiltration
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/17
tags:

logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  parent_build_script:
    ParentImage|re|i: '[\\/]target[\\/](debug|release)[\\/]build[\\/].+[\\/]build[-_]script[-_]build(\.exe)?$'
  child_git:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\git.exe'
      - '/git'
  exfil_cmds:
    CommandLine|contains:

level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR linux.auditd) AND (@Image:(*\\git.exe OR *\\Git.exe OR *\\GIT.EXE) OR @process.executable.path:*/git) AND (@ParentImage:(*\\target\\debug\\build\\*build-script-build* OR *\\target\\release\\build\\*build-script-build* OR *\\Target\\Debug\\Build\\*build-script-build*) OR @process.parent.executable.path:(*/target/debug/build/*build-script-build OR */target/release/build/*build-script-build OR */target/debug/build/*build_script_build OR */target/release/build/*build_script_build)) AND (@CommandLine:(*"diff HEAD^ HEAD"* OR *"--pretty=format:{\"commit\""* OR *"log -n 1"*) OR @process.command_line:(*"diff HEAD^ HEAD"* OR *"--pretty=format:{\"commit\""* OR *"log -n 1"*))

| ParentBaseFileName=/^build[-_]script[-_]build(\.exe)?$/i OR ParentImageFileName=/[\\\/]target[\\\/](debug|release)[\\\/]build[\\\/].+[\\\/]build[-_]script[-_]build/i
| regex("diff HEAD\\^ HEAD|--pretty=format:\\{\"commit\"|log -n 1", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |

    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"

   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"

| order by TimeGenerated desc

10 year old critical vulnerability in phpBB affecting tens of millions of users across thousands of forums

Aikido
2026-06-10 5 use cases 2 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Aikido Security discovered a critical unauthenticated authentication bypass in phpBB affecting tens of millions of users. A single HTTP request is all it takes to take over any account — a vulnerability that's been sitting in the codebase since 2014. Category: Vulnerabilities & Threats

CVEsCVE-2026-29199

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer). → [LLM] Vulnerable phpBB instance exposed to CVE-2026-29199 (auth-bypass → RCE)
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] phpBB web stack process spawns OS shell or download tool (RCE indicator)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] phpBB writable directory receives PHP/PHAR/PHTML file (post-RCE web shell drop)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Vulnerable phpBB instance exposed to CVE-2026-29199 (auth-bypass → RCE) AIWeaponization High
Identifies hosts running phpBB at or below 3.3.16 / 4.0.0-a2, which are vulnerable to the unauthenticated session-takeover-to-RCE chain disclosed by Aikido. Highest fidelity to the article — the patched version (3.3.17) and exact affected range are explicit. Rationale: Anchored on CVE-2026-29199 plus the article's explicit affected-version statement ("all versions up to and including 3.3.16 and 4.0.0-a2") and patched version 3.3.17. Software inventory + CVE join keeps this clean of generic phpBB noise.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • phpBB 3.3.17+ instance flagged because TVM has stale inventory data (delayed re-scan)
  • Test/lab phpBB instance intentionally kept on old version for exploit research
  • Vendor-bundled phpBB inside a Docker image where the host kernel sees the package but it is not internet-exposed
  • TVM signature match on a phpBB fork (e.g. phpBB3-style mods) that does not share the vulnerable code path
Suppression filter
| where SoftwareVersion !startswith "3.3.17" and SoftwareVersion !startswith "3.3.18"
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm phpBB version directly via the instance footer or `composer.lock` — TVM versioning sometimes lags. Determine if the forum is internet-facing and whether default-config member list (public) is enabled. 2) Contain: schedule emergency upgrade to 3.3.17 (or 4.x master) within 24h; if upgrade cannot happen immediately, place the instance behind WAF rule blocking unauthenticated POSTs to /ucp.php login/auth endpoints and rotate all admin/moderator passwords + invalidate sessions. 3) Hunt: pivot to UC2 + UC3 looking for in-the-wild exploitation indicators on the same host (web-shell drops in writable phpBB dirs, php-fpm spawning shells).

| project TimeGenerated, DeviceId, DeviceName, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate, CveId

phpBB writable directory receives PHP/PHAR/PHTML file (post-RCE web shell drop) AIInstallation Medium
Detects creation of executable PHP content under phpBB writable directories (cache/, store/, files/, ext/, images/avatars/upload/). Following the CVE-2026-29199 admin-takeover → RCE chain, the standard persistence move is to drop a web shell into one of these world-writable paths that PHP-FPM will execute. Rationale: Anchored on phpBB's well-known writable directory layout (cache/, store/, files/, ext/, images/avatars/upload/) and the article's RCE outcome. Constraining the writing process to PHP-handling web binaries removes most extension-install/backup noise.
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Admin uploads a legitimate phpBB extension into the ext/ directory via the ACP Extension Manager
  • phpBB auto-regenerates compiled twig templates as .php cache files under cache/production/
  • Backup/restore tool unpacks a board archive that contains the cache/ folder
  • CI/CD deploy job re-writing the phpBB tree, owned by the same uid as php-fpm
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("composer","ext_install","adm/index.php") and AccountName has_any ("root","admin","deploy"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the dropped file's SHA256 and decode/strstr it for eval/base64/assert/$_REQUEST patterns; correlate FolderPath with whether the host is the same one flagged by UC1. 2) Contain: isolate the host from the network, kill the PHP-FPM workers, snapshot for forensics, then rotate phpBB admin + DB credentials and invalidate all sessions (phpbb_sessions table). 3) Hunt: query the web access logs for POSTs to the dropped file's URL in the prior 30 days to scope attacker dwell time; pivot to UC3 on the same host to look for downstream shell spawns.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FileName matches regex @"(?i)\.(php|phar|phtml|php5|phps)$"
| where FolderPath matches regex @"(?i)(/|\\)(phpBB3|phpbb)(/|\\)(cache|store|files|ext|images/avatars/upload|images\\avatars\\upload)(/|\\)"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php-fpm","php-fpm7.4","php-fpm8.1","php-fpm8.2","php-fpm8.3","php-cgi","php-cgi.exe","httpd","apache2","nginx","w3wp.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RequestSourceIP
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType == "FileCreated" or EventType == "FileModified"
| where TargetFileName matches regex @"(?i)\.(php|phar|phtml|php5|phps)$"
| where TargetFilePath matches regex @"(?i)(/|\\)(phpBB3|phpbb)(/|\\)(cache|store|files|ext|images/avatars/upload|images\\avatars\\upload)(/|\\)"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("php-fpm","php-cgi","httpd","apache2","nginx","w3wp.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername

phpBB web stack process spawns OS shell or download tool (RCE indicator) AIExploitation Medium
Detects PHP-handling web server processes (php-fpm, php-cgi, apache2, httpd, nginx, w3wp.exe) spawning interactive shells or LOLBin downloaders. Following the CVE-2026-29199 auth-bypass → admin-RCE chain, this is the canonical post-exploitation execution shape. Rationale: phpBB runs on the PHP web stack; the article confirms admin-session takeover opens the door to RCE. Constraining the parent to PHP-handling web binaries and the child to shells/LOLBins is the canonical post-RCE shape for any PHP app, and on a host running phpBB this becomes high-fidelity for CVE-2026-29199 exploitation.
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • phpBB cron task shelling out to /usr/sbin/sendmail via PHP mail()
  • ImageMagick or GD image-resize pipeline invoking convert/identify subprocess for avatar uploads
  • Legitimate phpBB extension that invokes ClamAV (clamscan) on attachment upload
  • DevOps invoking phpBB ACP commands via php-cli through a wrapper script
  • Composer/git pull subprocess during extension installation by an admin
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/usr/sbin/sendmail","-t -i","phpmailer","clamscan","convert -resize","identify -format","composer install","composer update","git pull"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: examine the child command line for reverse-shell strings (bash -i, /dev/tcp/, python -c 'import socket'), curl/wget pulls of unknown IPs, or base64 payloads. Correlate the host with UC1 (vulnerable phpBB version). 2) Contain: snapshot the host for forensics, kill the offending PHP-FPM worker pool, isolate the web tier from the network, rotate phpBB admin credentials and DB password, invalidate sessions (TRUNCATE phpbb_sessions). 3) Hunt: pivot to UC2 for web-shell files written within ±30 minutes of this event; review outbound network from the host for the last 7 days for the destination IPs/domains seen in curl/wget commands; review web access logs for the request that immediately preceded the shell spawn.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php-fpm","php-fpm7.4","php-fpm8.1","php-fpm8.2","php-fpm8.3","php-cgi","php-cgi.exe","httpd","apache2","nginx","w3wp.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("bash","sh","dash","zsh","ksh","python","python3","perl","ruby","wget","curl","nc","ncat","socat","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/usr/sbin/sendmail","phpmailer","imagemagick","convert -"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("php-fpm","php-cgi","httpd","apache2","nginx","w3wp.exe")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("bash","sh","dash","zsh","ksh","python","python3","perl","ruby","wget","curl","nc","ncat","socat","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

HTTP POST to pheditor.php terminal handler (CVE-2026-48030 exploitation surface) AIDelivery Medium
Hunts inbound HTTP POSTs to the Pheditor terminal action handler at /pheditor.php. This is the single vulnerable endpoint identified in CVE-2026-48030; any POST with action=terminal from an unexpected source IP, user, or user-agent is worth triaging against the dir-parameter injection vector. Rationale: Article explicitly names pheditor.php as the vulnerable script and POST as the request method. Any POST to this endpoint should be reviewable since exploitation requires it. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jvc5-6g7q-c843
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate admin using the Pheditor terminal tab from corporate VPN
  • Authorized penetration tests against the application
  • Automated configuration management hitting the admin UI
  • Internal scanner discovering known admin endpoints
Suppression filter
| where SourceIP !in ("10.10.10.10","10.10.10.11") // sanctioned admin jump hosts
| where SourceUserName !in~ ("pheditor-admin","deploy-bot")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the SourceIP, SourceUserName and User-Agent. Verify the IP is on the admin allow-list and the session belongs to a sanctioned Pheditor admin. Decode the POST body and inspect the dir parameter for `;`, `|`, `$(`, backticks, `&&`, or `>` characters. Step 2 (contain): If dir contains shell metacharacters or the source is unauthorized, block the source IP at the WAF, invalidate the Pheditor session, and force a credential rotation for any account that authenticated. Step 3 (hunt): On the affected host, pivot to DeviceProcessEvents/ImProcessCreate for www-data spawning sh/bash/curl/wget within 30s of the POST, and DeviceFileEvents for new *.php files under /var/www. Confirm Pheditor version is in the vulnerable range (>=2.0.1, <=2.0.3) and upgrade.
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestURL has "pheditor.php"
| where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, DestinationIP, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestClientApplication, Message, DeviceAction, SourceUserName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Web server process (php-fpm/apache2/nginx) spawning shell or network tool as web user AIExploitation High
Hunts a php-fpm/apache2/httpd/nginx parent spawning sh, bash, dash, curl, wget, nc, python or perl under a web-server account (www-data/apache/nginx/daemon/nobody). This is the post-exploitation execution shape of CVE-2026-48030 - shell_exec() in pheditor.php invoking the attacker's injected command as the web user. Rationale: Article shows shell_exec() invoking the injected payload via cd $dir && command, which on Linux executes as the web-server account. The parent (php-fpm/apache2) + shell/network-tool child + web-user account triad is exactly the post-exploitation footprint. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jvc5-6g7q-c843
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • PHP application using system()/exec() for image conversion (ImageMagick) or PDF generation
  • Composer post-install scripts invoking shell as web user during deployments
  • Backup cron jobs running under www-data calling tar/curl
  • WordPress/Laravel plugins doing legitimate curl outbound calls
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("convert","gs ","wkhtmltopdf","composer"))
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/usr/bin/wkhtmltopdf","/usr/bin/convert","backup.sh"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Capture the full ProcessCommandLine of the child and the InitiatingProcessCommandLine of the parent. Look for `cd /something; <attacker_cmd>` or wget/curl to external IPs - the article's PoC pattern. Correlate within 30s back to any POST hitting pheditor.php from web access logs. Step 2 (contain): Isolate the host from the network, kill the offending process tree, and preserve memory for IR. Quarantine the Pheditor install pending upgrade out of the 2.0.1-2.0.3 vulnerable range. Step 3 (hunt): On the same host pivot to DeviceFileEvents for new *.php in /var/www, check ~/.ssh/authorized_keys for new entries, and review crontab/systemd for new persistence by www-data. Sweep peer web servers for the same parent/child pair.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php-fpm","php-fpm7.4","php-fpm8.0","php-fpm8.1","php-fpm8.2","apache2","httpd","nginx")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","curl","wget","nc","ncat","python","python3","perl","ruby")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName in~ ("www-data","apache","nginx","daemon","nobody","httpd")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("php-fpm","apache2","httpd","nginx")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("sh","bash","dash","curl","wget","nc","ncat","python","perl")
| where ActorUsername in~ ("www-data","apache","nginx","daemon","nobody","httpd")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

PHP webshell drop: web user writing .php to webroot post-exploitation AIInstallation High
Hunts FileCreated/FileModified events for *.php files inside /var/www, /srv/www, /usr/share/nginx, /var/html when the writer is a web-server process running as www-data/apache/nginx. The article's Step 5 PoC drops shell.php to /var/www/html via the dir injection - this UC catches that persistence artifact. Rationale: Article PoC Step 5 literally writes `<?php system($_GET[c]);?>` to /var/www/html/shell.php via dir injection. A .php file appearing under the webroot - written by the web-server user via shell/php parent - is the exact persistence artifact. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jvc5-6g7q-c843
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • WordPress/Drupal/Joomla plugin install or core update writing PHP files via the admin UI
  • Pheditor itself being used legitimately to save/edit a .php file (its purpose) - filter on known admin sessions
  • git clone/composer install run as www-data during in-place deployment
  • PHP opcache writing .php proxy files in /var/www/cache
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("wp-cli","drush","composer install","composer update"))
| where not (FolderPath has_any ("/wp-content/plugins/","/wp-content/upgrade/","/sites/all/modules/"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Read the newly-written .php file. Look for `system()`, `eval()`, `assert()`, `base64_decode`, `$_GET`/`$_POST` super-globals, `shell_exec` - classic webshell primitives. Hash it, compare against known webshell repos (PHP-Backdoors, p0wny-shell). Cross-reference timestamp with web access logs for POSTs to /pheditor.php. Step 2 (contain): Delete or quarantine the file, isolate the host, kill any active web-shell processes (pgrep for the file path). Reset Pheditor admin creds and rotate any secrets reachable from the webroot. Step 3 (hunt): Sweep entire /var/www for *.php files created or modified in the last 30 days by web user, diff against last-known-good Pheditor install. Pull web access logs for GET requests to the new file path - any `?c=` or `?cmd=` query strings confirm webshell usage. Check the same paths on sibling web servers.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FileName endswith ".php"
| where FolderPath has_any ("/var/www/","/srv/www/","/usr/share/nginx/","/var/html/")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php-fpm","php-fpm7.4","php-fpm8.0","php-fpm8.1","php-fpm8.2","apache2","httpd","nginx","sh","bash","dash")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName in~ ("www-data","apache","nginx","daemon","nobody","httpd")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFileName endswith ".php"
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("/var/www/","/srv/www/","/usr/share/nginx/","/var/html/")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("php-fpm","apache2","httpd","nginx","sh","bash","dash")
| where ActorUsername in~ ("www-data","apache","nginx","daemon","nobody")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActorUsername, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
